messages:
dana: Heads up — TechCo reported 5xxs from the hosted inference endpoint about 11:02 UTC. Customer says the errors started suddenly and are affecting generate and chat calls. Request IDs: rQf9-01, rQf9-02, rQf9-03.

sam: Thanks. Can you paste an example curl and any response body/headers (correlation-id)? Also which model and route?

dana: Sure — hitting /v1/generate on hosted, model: redwood-3b. Example:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"hi"}'
```

Response: 502 Bad Gateway

```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
x-request-id: rQf9-01

{"error":"control_plane_dependency_failure","detail":"auth/session service returned 502","code":502}
```

sam: x-request-id present, good. "auth/session service returned 502" — suggests control-plane dependency. Maria, any spikes on routing-policy or config-db?

maria: I'm seeing elevated latency to config-db pool and routing-policy timeouts around 11:00-11:10 UTC. Metrics: configdb p95 conn latency tripled, routing-policy 504 rate: ~8%. Auth/session had a handful of 502s and a backend timeout (upstream read).

ankur: Likely cascade: config DB slow => routing policy times out => control plane tries auth/session and hits backlog. Two things to check: 1) connection pool exhaustion on configdb, 2) routing-policy circuit breaker tuning.

sam: Can you grab control-plane logs for x-request-id rQf9-01 and a few around it and post the small excerpt? Also kube events for config-db pods.

dana: Pasted logs snippet below (sanitized):

```
[11:02:12] control-plane ERROR request=rQf9-01 upstream=auth/session status=502 error="upstream read timeout"
[11:02:12] control-plane WARN routing-policy request=rQf9-01 backend=rpc timeout=1200ms
[11:02:13] control-plane ERROR configdb query=GetRoutingByKey err="context deadline exceeded"
```

kubectl get pods -n infra:
```
NAME                        READY   STATUS    RESTARTS
configdb-0                  1/1     Running   0
configdb-1                  1/1     Running   0
routing-policy-6b8f9        2/2     Running   3
routing-policy-6b8f9        2/2     Running   2
```

sam: Noted restarts on routing-policy pods, looks like retries. Maria, can you check DB connection pool stats (active conns, waiters)?

maria: DB pool peak active=260, configured max=256 — we hit the ceiling and saw queuing. Also observed occasional slow queries on the routing table scan. Looks like a slow maintenance job overlapped traffic spike.

ankur: Plan: immediate mitigation: 1) enable routing-policy cached fallback so control-plane can use cached routes for 30s (reduces DB reads), 2) increase DB pool to 320 temporarily, 3) restart routing-policy pods one at a time to clear stuck goroutines. Who can make the config change?

sam: I'm on-call, will trigger the cached-fallback feature flag and scale DB pool. Dana, please notify TechCo of mitigation in progress and ask for any traffic pattern changes.

deploy-bot: Initiating rollout: feature-flag (routing-policy-cached-fallback) -> canary 1/4 -> started. :rocket:

sam: kubectl patch cm control-plane-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"routing_policy.cache_enabled":"true","routing_policy.cache_ttl_ms":"30000"}}'

maria: DB pool increased via launchpad: set max_connections=320 on configdb cluster; applying now. Also killing the single stuck routing-policy pod to force warm restart.

deploy-bot: Canary completed: 1/4 -> 2/4 -> 4/4. Feature flag active.

dana: Sent update to TechCo: "We identified a cascade from a configuration DB slowdown causing routing policy timeouts which then surfaced as control-plane 502s. We're rolling a temporary cached fallback and increasing DB pool; monitoring. ETA 10-15m."

sam: Post-mitigation checks: observed 5xxs drop to zero in the last 3 minutes, routing-policy 504 rate down to 0.5%, configdb p95 latencies returning to baseline.

ankur: Good. Root cause: nightly maintenance job created a spike in locking/slow queries and exhausted DB pool. Action items: 1) add circuit-breaker + cached fallback permanently, 2) increase pool headroom, 3) schedule maintenance during low traffic, 4) add alert for DB pool saturation.

maria: I'll open infra tickets: INFRA-1893 (DB pool headroom), INFRA-1894 (query optimization for routing table), INFRA-1895 (alert: db.pool.waiters > 10 for 2m).

sam: I'll update the runbook and add a quick playbook: commands to flip cached-fallback, scale DB, restart pods, and required telemetry.

dana: TechCo confirmed service resumed and thanked us. Closing loop. :tada:

sam: Leaving follow-up: We'll run a postmortem doc tomorrow with timeline + load graphs. For now marking incident resolved and lowering pager noise.

ankur: Thx all. Proposed next step: limit long-running maintenance on routing table during peak hours and add sample queries to reproduce the slow path.

maria: I'll attach metrics and flamegraphs to the ticket.

deploy-bot: Deployment notes: feature-flag rollback window: 30m. No rollback required.

sam: Closing thread — please add any leftover notes. :white_check_mark:
